texts.facts: The present suit has been filed by the plaintiff against the defendant for recovery of Rs. 25,352/- alongwith interest. FACTS AS PER THE PLAINT : 2. In brief, the facts of the case as per the plaint are that the plaintiff company sells and supplies Potato, Onion etc. to the other businessman like: to the owners of the canteen, sweets shop; on the other hand, the defendant- a Food Canteen Rohini Courts is being run by its said owner/in-charge Delhi Alu Company vs Food Canteen Rohini Court on 25 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124414798/ 1 with the name and style "Food Canteen Rohini Courts" as such plaintiff used to supply potatoes and onion to the defendant as well. On 19.02.2020, 12.02.2020, 16.03.2020, 16.01.2020, 28.02.2020 & 02.03.2020, plaintiff has supplied the potatoes and onion to the defendant but total amount of Rs. 25,352/- is still due upon the defendant. It is further stated that despite of several visits, telephonic calls and requests made by the plaintiff, the defendant has not paid the said amount Hence, the present suit. (I) Pass a decree for recovery of Rs. 25,352/- alongwith further interest @ 24% per annum since the dates of bills till the realizatioin of amount of the plaintiff in favour of plaintiff and against the defendant. CS No. 293/2022 Delhi Alu Company Vs. Food Canteen Rohini Court Page No. 2 of 21 (II) Award future and pendente-lite interest in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant at the rate of 15% per annum. (III) Cost of the suit and other expenses bear by the plaintiff in favour of plaintiff and against the defendant . (IV) Any other Relief. DEFENCE :- 4. The WS has been filed on behalf of defendant wherein it was averred that the defendant was running a business of food vending, establishing under the name and style "M/s Jagjeet Caterers" and accordingly, is running the business in the second floor, Rohini Courts. It was further averred that no such business activities have run/taken place between the parties. There is no documents placed on record which show any business relations between the plaintiff and defendant or that any transaction/business/trading activity as alleged has been done or taken place between plaintiff and defendant. It was further averred that neither any agreement has been executed/entered into between the parties nor any order has been placed by the defendant. The plaintiff has not placed on record the statement of account or confirmation of account pertaining to or showing any liabilities upon the defendant towards the plaintiff. It was further submitted that none of the bills pertains to the defendant as well as no signatures of the receiver of the goods have been obtained on the bills/or reflecting on the bills. It was further averred that no cause of action CS No. 293/2022 Delhi Alu Company Vs. Food Canteen Rohini Court Page No. 3 of 21 has arisen against the defendant. On merits, the contents of the plaint denied in toto. 2 5. Replication to WS of defendant was filed in the present case. In replication the contents of plaint are reaitrated and denied the story of defendant. OPP. (II) Costs and any other relief. In support of plaintiff's case, proprietor of the plaintiff company Sh. texts.arguments: 13. It is argued by Ld. Counsel for plaintiff that plaintiff has proved his case upon preponderance of probabilities and defendant has failed to raise any doubt over the testimony of PW-1. Per contra, it is argued on behalf of defendant that plaintiff has failed to prove any case against the defendant as he failed to prove that he delivered any goods to the defendant at any point of time. Moreover, it is also argued on behalf of defendant that plaintiff even failed to produce any document which can show that there were any business relations between the parties. Even the plaintiff failed to establish the identity of the defendant or his firm as the name of defendant is Jagjit and not Jagdip. Further, defendant is running his business under the name and style of M/s. Jagjeet Caterers. As laid down in Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research v. Jaspal Singh, (2009) 7 SCC 330, the burden which ought to be discharged in civil proceedings in not as strict as in criminal cases and in order for any party to succeed, he/it is required to prove his/its case on the preponderance of probabilities. In civil proceedings, a mere preponderance of probability is sufficient, and the defendant is not necessarily entitled to the benefit of every reasonable doubt; but in criminal proceedings, the persuasion of guilt must amount to such a moral certainty as convinces the mind of the court, as a reasonable man, beyond all reasonable doubt." 15. The Court emphasized that where invoices remain uncontested or insufficiently disputed, and where the defendant does not bring forth any evidence to establish fabrication or discrepancy, such bills must ordinarily be accepted as genuine. The principle is that a party who fails to produce the best possible evidence must be presumed to be avoiding it because it would go against him. 43. A bare plea or a simple denial, without proof, holds no evidentiary value in the eyes of the law, justifying the court in favoring the opposite party's probable case. 44. Having weighed the testimonies and documents produced, the Court finds that the plaintiff's version is coherent, consistent and supported by primary evidence in the form of original bills.
